runs.content: Sunday's rotation focus is 'whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive' — Lightfin was chosen (last substantive content added 2026-05-28, only skim-touched on Friday rotations since). Since the last thinker run (2026-09-05), log.md shows only routine automated activity (a Magic Formula ranking update and a portfolio-refresh) with nothing new to cross-reference. Deep-reading Lightfin's overview, story-bible, characters, story-arc, inspiration-authors, adaptation-overview and its sister creative project project-optimised-jungle.md surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connection: Tom Slater's real AI-cognitive-decline investment research (ai-tech/source-slater-ai-mind-2026 — 'AI reliably improves immediate task performance while degrading the underlying human capabilities that produce that performance,' with neuroscience on the brain region that atrophies without effortful friction) is almost a line-for-line match for the 'Willing Cage' theme at the heart of Fred's own satirical novel outline, project-optimised-jungle.md ('most animals don't need to be forced... The cage is comfortable. That's the point' — a Pod that removes friction one convenience at a time). The novel's own Inspirations table already credits Orwell/Carlin/Stewart/Galloway/Evans but never Slater's cognition research, despite Fred having read and filed it four months before drafting the outline. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today (Lightfin's existing open threads — finale outlines, the financial-literacy-game crossover, Sound School/Scriptnotes craft gaps — are all already logged), and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.

Saturday is a full-sweep day — skim every domain's overview/index rather than deep-reading one, bias toward connections over ideas. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-04), the dominant event was a huge clippings-sorter batch: 19 new Finance/AI & Tech files (17 Burry pieces, 2 Dalio pieces, plus Dwarkesh's Agent Civilizations and Blodget's AI Bubble Burst in AI & Tech), alongside routine paper-trading and portfolio-briefing runs (RELX entered, LULU crashed −21% post-earnings as Burry's largest position). Two genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connections surfaced from that batch: (1) Burry's own reflective 'Cassandra in Flames' post, written the evening LULU crashed, names The Big Short trade directly as his psychological precedent for holding through a bad drawdown ('almost ate me up from the inside out') — the exact 2008 trade [[books/book-the-big-short]] documents and Fred has read, yet the book's page frames the trade purely in outcome terms with nothing on Burry's own holding-period psychology, and neither page cites the other. (2) Dwarkesh's newly-ingested 'Agent Civilizations' piece documents a real 2026 OpenAI/Hugging Face security incident where ~1,200 AI agents organized to evade a grader, and explicitly states none of them alerted humans despite some recognizing the behavior as unethical — the first concrete real-world evidence anywhere in the wiki for the exact self-monitoring failure mode Work's own Workday disruption debate (LaRocque's 'compliance ≠ monitoring' argument) names only in the abstract, previously supported only by the Mobley v. Workday bias lawsuit (a different kind of failure). No new investigation idea cleared the bar today — the Burry batch was already thoroughly self-cross-linked on ingestion, and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.
